clue.text: See 6
Ritual power surrounding wicked metal bracelet

indicators.note: surrounding tells us the word for ritual power is wrapped around the word for wicked

parts.note: mana is the supernatural power invoked in Polynesian ritual and belief
ill can mean evil or wicked, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: A wicked ritual involves a powerful metal bracelet.
explanation.definitionFit: A manilla is a metal ring or bracelet once worn in West Africa and used as currency.

clue.text: Actress's scare, forgetting Kipling's lines

indicators.note: forgetting tells us the poem's title is dropped from the word for scare

parts.note: to scare someone is to terrify them
If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: An actress gets a fright and forgets her lines from Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Actress's stands for 'is', a link. Ellen Terry was a celebrated Victorian stage actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen Terry was a leading English actress of the Victorian stage.

clue.text: Assigned to the Guardian perhaps, in theory

definitions.meaning: a journalist employed by a newspaper such as the Guardian works on that publication
something true in theory looks right in writing but may fail in practice

explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is on a newspaper, and a plan sound in theory looks good when written down.

clue.text: Cluster of flowers seen in spring — ten in the Luxembourg gardens

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
the Luxembourg Gardens are in Paris, where ten is dix in French

explanation.surface: A gardener spots spring blooms in the Paris park.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jardin du Luxembourg is a famous public park in Paris, so the number is given in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A spadix is a fleshy spike crowded with small flowers, as in the arum lily.

clue.text: The old man wants a dish

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old-fashioned British slang, for father, colloquially the old man

explanation.surface: Dad is hungry and asks for a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A patera is a broad shallow dish used in ancient Rome for pouring libations.

clue.text: The Lord's wicket? Mud! How to work out way of dealing with rain-affected game?

definitions.text: way of dealing with rain-affected game

indicators.note: working out the letters means solving them by rearranging into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive apostrophe giving no letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddy pitch at Lord's raises the question of how to settle a game ruined by rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground. Cricket matches cut short by rain are decided by a statistical formula named after its two inventors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duckworth-Lewis method recalculates a cricket target when rain shortens a one-day match.

clue.text: Possible reason for chap giving kiss? Love is!

parts.note: X is the conventional written kiss
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: Why would a man give a kiss? Because he is in love!
explanation.walkthrough: 'chap' looks like a man, but here it is chapped skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerosis is abnormal dryness of the skin, which can leave it cracked and chapped.

clue.text: Fellow to flash around the Oval, say, creating a story

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: around tells us the flash word is placed round the playing area

parts.note: a spark is a flash of light
the Oval is a London cricket ground, an example of a playing field

explanation.surface: A man lights fireworks around the Oval cricket ground and makes up a tale about it.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; 'creating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield Park is a novel by Jane Austen, a long story.

clue.text: Remarkable person in arithmetic only, maybe?

parts.note: one can mean single or only, as in the one and only
arithmetic is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and 'rithmetic

explanation.surface: Someone notable only in their sums, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are the basics of schooling: reading, writing and arithmetic, so R stands for arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for an outstanding or unique person or thing.

clue.text: What may involve modelling ceramics and tar?

definitions.text: What may involve modelling ceramics and tar?

parts.words: What may involve modelling ceramics and tar?
parts.note: the fine art of shaping three-dimensional materials such as clay and pottery, with tar a reshuffled hint at the second word

explanation.walkthrough: Plastic here means mouldable; TAR rearranged hints at the second word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The plastic arts are those involving modelling or shaping material, such as sculpture and ceramics.

clue.text: Cheeky youngster hanging around station to give trouble

indicators.note: hanging around tells us the youngster word sits round the station word

parts.note: a pup is an impudent young man
to station something is to place or lay it

explanation.surface: A cheeky kid loiters at the railway station to cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To play up is to misbehave or to cause pain or difficulty, as a bad knee does.

clue.text: There's little right in the woman with desire to be nagging

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation sits inside the pronoun for the woman

parts.note: she refers to the woman
R is the short form of right
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: A woman with little right on her side who wants things is a nag.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewish describes a bad-tempered, nagging manner, like that of a scold.

clue.text: Nancy restricted by wind — medicine needed

indicators.note: restricted by tells us Nancy is enclosed within the wind word

parts.note: to wind is to coil
Nancy Astor was the first woman to sit in the British House of Commons

explanation.surface: Nancy, laid up with wind, needs a dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like flatulence, but it is the verb, to coil.
explanation.definitionFit: Castor oil was a classic, foul-tasting laxative medicine.

clue.text: Celtic symbols of danger in forged steel frame

indicators.note: frame tells us the reshaped metal letters surround the danger word
forged means shaped by hammering, so the metal's letters are reshaped

parts.note: risk means danger

explanation.surface: Celtic emblems warning of danger are set in a frame of wrought steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' turns STEEL into TELES, which frames RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: A triskele is a Celtic motif of three spirals or legs radiating from a centre.

clue.text: Supplies a reduced value of statistical significance

parts.note: RMS abbreviates root mean square, an important statistical value

explanation.surface: A statistician provides a cut-down figure of significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' signals the abbreviation of root mean square.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm is to supply with weapons, so arms means supplies with weaponry.

clue.text: Ship's senior officer?

definitions.meaning: short for brigadier, a senior army rank

explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted ship, and brig is short for brigadier, a senior army officer.

clue.text: Mean to have egg in bar — or something much more substantial?

indicators.note: in tells us the mean-plus-egg pair goes inside the bar word

parts.note: but means except, as does bar
low means base or mean
O looks like an egg

explanation.surface: A stingy person has an egg in the pub, rather than a big feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is 'except', BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowout is a large, lavish meal, far more substantial than an egg.

clue.text: A hindrance to teacher?

parts.note: a block is an obstacle or hindrance
a head is a headteacher

explanation.surface: Something that gets in the way of a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce or stupid pupil would be a burden for any teacher.

clue.text: Actors given guidance made a special move

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play
led means guided

explanation.surface: Actors directed to perform a special manoeuvre on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is a special chess move of king and rook together.

clue.text: Take care putting clubs down in bridge

indicators.note: putting tells us one letter is relocated within the word
down, in a down clue, says the letter moves lower in the word

parts.note: caution is a warning to take care
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Be careful when you lay down clubs in a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... down' moves the C of CAUTION further down, giving AUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is the form of bridge that preceded contract bridge.

clue.text: Not much light to take picture before noon

parts.note: a photo is a picture

explanation.surface: Take a photograph before midday, when the light is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A photon is a single quantum of light, the smallest amount there is.

clue.text: She may be in this store

definitions.text: She may be in this store

parts.words: She may be in this store
parts.note: the pronoun is also the title of a novel by H. Rider Haggard, which a seller of books would stock

explanation.definitionFit: A bookshop stocks novels, among them Haggard's novel titled She.

clue.text: Unfair dealer getting rid of a year's tat

indicators.note: getting rid of tells us a letter is removed

parts.note: Shylock is the moneylender in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, a byword for a ruthless dealer
Y abbreviates year

explanation.surface: A crooked trader clears out a year's worth of junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Schlock or shlock is cheap, shoddy goods, the same as tat.

clue.text: See 6
Pounds subsequently invested in fuel for security

indicators.note: invested in tells us the pieces are put inside the fuel word

parts.note: coal is a fuel
L abbreviates pounds, from Latin libra
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: Money later put into fuel stocks as a safeguard.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as security for a loan.

clue.text: Scrap Church festival

definitions.meaning: Whitsun, the Christian feast of Pentecost

explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, and Whit is short for Whitsun, Pentecost.

clue.text: It's a new drug that you may take as a relaxant

definitions.text: that you may take as a relaxant

parts.note: 'tis is an old contraction of it is
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A new drug is being sold as a way to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal tea, often drunk to soothe and relax.

clue.text: Funny boy? Such may be the favourite

parts.note: odd means funny or strange
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A strange lad is tipped as the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on describes betting odds shorter than evens, typical of the race favourite.
